title: Best Money Belt 2026: 5 RFID Belts Compared
description: Eagle Creek, Lewis N. Clark, Alpine Rivers, Peak Gear and Zero Grid compared on RFID lining, mesh breathability and how visible each one is under a thin shirt.
lede: This guide compares 5 options using published specifications, manufacturer documentation and independent reviews.
methodology: This comparison is desk research. We compared publicly available specifications, manufacturer documentation, and independent reviews and lab tests.

sections.heading: Around-waist vs. leg vs. neck in 2026
paragraphs: Three carry positions emerged. Around-waist belts (Eagle Creek, Lewis N. Clark, Peak Gear, Zero Grid) are the most common — hidden under shirts. Leg wallets (Alpine Rivers) tie to calf or thigh; invisible but harder to access. Neck pouches (not covered here) work for under-shirt carry but bounce while walking.

RFID blocking is now standard. All five here block RFID at card position. The differentiator is breathability — mesh-back belts (Lewis N. Clark, Zero Grid) are noticeably more comfortable in hot weather.

sections.heading: Visibility and comfort
paragraphs: Visibility under a thin shirt, as owners describe it: Zero Grid and Lewis N. Clark disappear completely, Eagle Creek and Peak Gear leave a slight outline, and the Alpine Rivers leg wallet is invisible simply because it never sits at the waist.

Skin irritation on long trips tracks the backing material. The mesh-backed Lewis N. Clark and Zero Grid draw almost no complaints. The non-mesh Eagle Creek and Peak Gear draw reports of mild redness after consecutive days of wear, as does the Alpine Rivers band where it sits on the calf.

faqs.a: Not in known pickpocket cities (Rome, Barcelona, Paris, Buenos Aires, Bangkok). For low-pickpocket destinations (Helsinki, Reykjavik), a regular front-pocket wallet is fine.

faqs.q: Can I put my passport in a money belt?
faqs.a: Yes — all five here fit a passport. The Eagle Creek and Peak Gear belts are designed specifically with passport-sized compartments. Avoid bulky-folded passports; lay flat.

faqs.q: Will TSA flag a money belt at the airport?
faqs.a: No — money belts pass through metal detectors normally if you remove your watch (RFID blocking is foil-thin metal, not magnetic). Pat-downs don't differentiate it from a regular belt.

eagle-creek-undercover-belt.review: Eagle Creek Undercover Money Belt is the industry standard. Moisture-wicking back (though not full mesh), adjustable elastic, fits passport plus cards and cash. Used by serious travelers for 25+ years. The slight outline through thin shirts is the only downside.
cons: Not full mesh — warmer in summer

lewis-n-clark-rfid-belt.review: Lewis N. Clark RFID Money Belt has the mesh-back design that makes it the most comfortable option here. RFID-blocking fabric, breathable nylon mesh, passport-sized compartment. Anti-theft strap design. Invisible through thin shirts. Best for travel in hot climates where you wear a money belt 12+ hours/day.
pros: Mesh back invisible under thin shirts
cons: Less rigid than Eagle Creek for carrying coins

alpine-rivers-leg-wallet.review: Alpine Rivers Leg Wallet is the answer if you absolutely want no bulge visible. Worn on calf or thigh under pants, breathable mesh back, two compartments. Trade-off: accessing it means lifting your pants — fine for a hotel reset, awkward at a café register.

peak-gear-rfid-belt.review: Peak Gear RFID Money Belt is the lifetime-warranty pick. RFID-blocking, moisture-wicking, expandable, includes a passport scanner card. Comfortable enough but not the best in any single category. Best if you want one-and-done backed by warranty.

zero-grid-money-belt.review: Zero Grid Money Belt fits under the thinnest shirts. Ripstop nylon body, RFID-blocking, mesh back. Best for travelers who wear fitted shirts where the Eagle Creek outline would be visible. Compact volume means smaller passport-cards-cash capacity than competitors.

offerNotes.eagle-creek-undercover-belt: Classic and Hidden Pocket versions exist — Classic is the standard.
offerNotes.lewis-n-clark-rfid-belt: Mesh Back is the version with full mesh — confirm before buying.
offerNotes.alpine-rivers-leg-wallet: Use over thinner pants/skirts; layered over thicker pants creates visible bulge.
offerNotes.peak-gear-rfid-belt: Passport scanner card is a marketing nod — actual security depends on the belt's RFID lining.
offerNotes.zero-grid-money-belt: Doesn't hold large foreign-currency bills folded once — fold twice to fit.

pinDescription: Here's the invisible one for hot climates — and the leg wallet for truly hidden carry.

recommendedFor.label: Long-haul travelers visiting multiple pickpocket-heavy cities
recommendedFor.reason: Eagle Creek's 25-year track record and adjustable elastic make it the dependable all-day workhorse across multi-city itineraries.

recommendedFor.label: Backpackers and tourists in tropical or summer destinations
recommendedFor.reason: The full mesh back stays invisible under thin shirts and prevents the skin irritation that non-mesh belts cause after 12+ hours in 80°F+ heat.

recommendedFor.label: Undercover travelers who refuse any visible bulge under clothing
recommendedFor.reason: Worn on calf or thigh under pants, it creates zero waistband outline — the only option that's truly undetectable even in fitted trousers.

recommendedFor.label: Budget-conscious travelers who want a one-and-done purchase
recommendedFor.reason: The lifetime warranty means you buy once; the included passport scanner card adds value that comparable belts don't offer at this price.

recommendedFor.label: Fashion-forward travelers wearing slim-fit or tailored shirts
recommendedFor.reason: Zero Grid's slimmest ripstop nylon profile disappears under even the most form-fitting shirts where thicker belts leave a visible outline.
